inspection_summary: Inspected all 927 normalized lines. The survey develops RH through the zeta function's analytic/arithmetic dual description, prime-zero explicit formulas, equivalent reformulations, spectral and approximation programs, random-matrix evidence, families of L-functions, and the Landau-Siegel obstruction. The text is semantically rich but its two-column extraction interleaves columns and several displays have damaged glyphs, so units relying on exact formulas retain scan-verification notes.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, motivation, and visual introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces RH and the zeta function amid publication metadata, workshop history, and plots whose visual content is not fully represented by the text layer.

sections_inspected.label: Analytic continuation, Euler product, and prime-zero bridge
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents the completed functional equation, Euler product, zero strip, and explicit formula connecting primes to zeros.

sections_inspected.label: Initial equivalent criteria and Möbius route
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts RH as prime-counting and Möbius-sum bounds, then records why the strongest elementary-looking Mertens route fails.

sections_inspected.label: Subsequent analytic progress and evidence for RH
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Surveys approximate functional equations, moment and growth bounds, computational/density evidence, and probabilistic or regularity heuristics.

sections_inspected.label: Spectral, Fourier, probabilistic, and functional-analytic approaches
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces Hilbert-Polya, Polya's real-zero Fourier-transform program, a Brownian-bridge representation, and Nyman-Beurling approximation criteria.

sections_inspected.label: Weil explicit formula and positivity criteria
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Expresses prime-zero duality and turns RH into positivity of test-function sums, including Li's discrete coefficient criterion.

sections_inspected.label: Trace formula, false spectral identification, and elementary equivalences
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Continues Selberg's trace formula, diagnoses spurious computed eigenvalues, compares trace and explicit formulas, and lists cross-representation RH criteria.

sections_inspected.label: Other zeta and L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Generalizes the RH template through Euler products, functional equations, number fields, modular forms, elliptic curves, Langlands, and Selberg-style axioms.

sections_inspected.label: Random-matrix bridge and pair correlation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects zero spacings with GUE statistics while distinguishing statistical spectral evidence from an actual operator.

sections_inspected.label: Computations and moment models
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports high-zero numerical confirmation and transfers characteristic-polynomial moment calculations to conjectures for zeta values.

sections_inspected.label: Families and symmetry types
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses finite-field monodromy and Haar ensembles to organize L-function families and predict low zeros, moments, values, and central vanishing.

sections_inspected.label: Class numbers and the Landau-Siegel conspiracy
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Links exceptional real zeros to class numbers, repulsion, ineffectivity, sieve constants, and an alternative zero-spacing hypothesis.

sections_inspected.label: Threshold obstructions, multiplicity amplification, and Iwaniec's program
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows how tiny improvements in gaps or nonvanishing would remove exceptional zeros and how forced central multiplicity can tame Möbius through families.

sections_inspected.label: Conclusion and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts irregular L-function zeros with classical analytic zeros, argues for an arithmetic/family-based route, and closes with acknowledgements and references interleaved by the two-column extraction.

accepted_units.title: The zeta function becomes a global analytic object
accepted_units.why_material: The Dirichlet series is introduced together with continuation beyond its convergence half-plane and a functional equation, separating the initial representation from the global object studied by RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed symmetric completion appears later in the extracted reading order at lines 95-100 because of page layout.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on prose plus a partially degraded displayed series; verify the display against the scan for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Completion exposes reflection symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplying zeta by gamma, power-of-pi, and polynomial factors packages the functional equation as xi(s)=xi(1-s), the symmetry that organizes the critical strip.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the display promised in the preceding-page prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formula is legible in substance but has layout artifacts; exact normalization is scan-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Euler product translates unique factorization into analysis
accepted_units.why_material: The product over primes turns arithmetic factorization into a zero-free analytic statement and motivates using zeta to study prime distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage moves from Euler's product to the Gauss-Legendre prime-counting problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual content is recoverable from prose; displayed factors should be checked before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Prime-counting fluctuations are encoded by complex zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The explicit formula for the Chebyshev function makes individual zeros contribute oscillatory terms of size controlled by their real parts, explaining why zero location governs the prime number theorem error.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes convergence cautions and the definition of the zero sum; the right column begins the historical PNT conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the displayed explicit formula and von Mangoldt notation; several symbols are text-layer damaged, so exact coefficients need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: RH as square-root-scale prime-counting error
accepted_units.why_material: The survey states the direct operational equivalence between RH and a near-square-root error term for prime counting, then notes that direct control of pi(x) offers no evident new route to the zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is interleaved with the left-column tail of the explicit formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent is recoverable as 1/2+epsilon despite a damaged epsilon glyph; the integral display needs formula-safe rendering.

accepted_units.title: Möbius cancellation reframes RH but the sharp pointwise route fails
accepted_units.why_material: The reciprocal Euler product converts RH into cancellation of the Möbius summatory function via Dirichlet-series convergence; the stronger Mertens conjecture would imply RH but was disproved, isolating a tempting yet invalid strengthening.
accepted_units.context_note: Two-column extraction interrupts the Mertens conclusion with historical anecdotes; line 230 completes the statement that the conjectured sharp bound is likely false.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose mechanism is clear; exact series and bound symbols carry OCR risk.

accepted_units.title: Zero counting supplies the natural local spacing scale
accepted_units.why_material: The functional symmetry, zero-counting asymptotic, argument term, and resulting average gap 2pi/log T provide the normalization later used in random-matrix comparisons.
accepted_units.context_note: The span also recalls the first zeros and Riemann's estimate for the argument term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The asymptotic display is recoverable but formula punctuation and fractions require scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Functional symmetry yields convexity, arithmetic sums improve it
accepted_units.why_material: The account separates a general complex-analytic growth bound from Weyl's sharper bound obtained through exponential-sum structure, illustrating how arithmetic input can beat symmetry-only control.
accepted_units.context_note: Historical material and evidence bullets are interleaved across the page columns.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Growth exponents and epsilon notation are formula-dependent but readable in context.

accepted_units.title: Different evidence channels support RH with different force
accepted_units.why_material: The survey distinguishes finite zero verification, concentration near the line, proved on-line proportions, derivative-zero evidence, random-sign heuristics, and expected prime regularity rather than treating them as a single proof signal.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage includes an explicitly failed attempted converse-to-Rolle strategy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-grounded; numerical thresholds are historically dated and should be treated only as claims in this 2003 source.

accepted_units.title: The completed zeta function appears as a Brownian-bridge moment
accepted_units.why_material: A probabilistic identity represents xi as an expectation of a power of a Brownian-bridge range, supplying an unexpected alternative representation without itself resolving zero location.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is interleaved with the end of the evidence list and the start of Hilbert-Polya.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition of the random variable is display-dependent and should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Make RH automatic by realizing zero ordinates as a Hermitian spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Hilbert-Polya reframes a zero-location theorem as construction of a natural self-adjoint operator, so reality follows structurally from spectral theory.
accepted_units.context_note: The source emphasizes that this is a repeatedly attempted program, not an identified operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; the precise relation between eigenvalues and ordinates is stated clearly.

accepted_units.title: RH as density of fractional-part generators
accepted_units.why_material: Nyman-Beurling replaces zero location by density in L2, and later reformulations make it a weighted approximation of 1 by zeta times finite Dirichlet polynomials, yielding a quantitative distance sequence.
accepted_units.context_note: The two-column extraction interleaves this right-column development with Polya's left-column Fourier program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core equivalences are readable, but norms, infima, and the lower-bound display are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Fourier transform turns RH into membership in a real-zero class
accepted_units.why_material: The even real Xi function and its explicit Fourier transform motivate classifying kernels whose transforms have only real zeros; de Bruijn's theorem supplies a prototype sufficient-condition mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines from the Nyman-Beurling column are interleaved in the same physical span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact kernel and theorem hypotheses are display-heavy and need scan verification; the strategic transformation is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Explicit-formula duality turns RH into positivity
accepted_units.why_material: Weil's prime-zero explicit formula converts RH into positivity for an admissible class of test functions, while Li compresses this to positivity of a distinguished coefficient sequence whose missing geometric meaning is itself a strategic gap.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit carried as written; the span contains both criteria and begins an interleaved Selberg-trace column.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Substantive prose is recoverable, but the explicit formula and Li coefficients require scan verification before exact mathematical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Admissible test functions mediate prime-zero positivity
accepted_units.why_material: The source gives the test-function hypotheses, Fourier transform, prime-side sum, and zero-side sum that make Weil's criterion an engineered positivity problem rather than a bare restatement of zero location.
accepted_units.context_note: This mechanism is contained within the broader carried v1 positivity unit and is retained separately because its test-function interface is reusable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent and affected by two-column ordering; exact gamma and normalization terms need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Trace formulas resemble explicit formulas without identifying zeta zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Selberg's trace formula offers a genuine spectral/geometric duality resembling the prime-zero explicit formula, but the apparent occurrence of zeta zeros in computed eigenvalue lists came from pseudo cusp forms, warning that formal resemblance and numerical coincidence are insufficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The span deliberately includes the trace-formula setup omitted from the narrower carried false-friend unit; right-column equivalences are interleaved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact trace terms and eigenvalue parametrization are display-sensitive; the false-identification diagnosis is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: RH survives translation into series decay, matrix determinants, and divisor inequalities
accepted_units.why_material: Three easy-to-state equivalences demonstrate that logically exact reformulations can occupy very different representational domains without automatically exposing a productive proof mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: The equivalence column is interleaved with the continuation of Selberg's trace formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formulas have degraded glyphs; use the unit for representational comparison unless checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Spurious spectral matches do not realize Hilbert-Polya
accepted_units.why_material: Computed coincidences between modular Laplacian eigenvalues and zeta or Dirichlet-L zero ordinates were artifacts of pseudo cusp forms; the episode isolates the difference between a legitimate spectral realization and a numerical false friend.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit carried as written; interpreting it safely requires the Selberg-trace setup from lines 381-459.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The diagnosis is prose-grounded; exact eigenvalues and trace-formula context remain scan/formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Euler product plus functional equation defines the RH candidate template
accepted_units.why_material: Dirichlet, number-field, modular, and elliptic examples motivate a broader class of L-functions, while Langlands and Selberg's axioms frame classification by shared arithmetic and symmetry structures rather than by surface formulas.
accepted_units.context_note: Page-column interleaving causes elliptic-curve continuation text to appear before its full left-column construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual classification is prose-supported; individual Euler products and completed functions require formula checking.

accepted_units.title: Local point counts assemble an elliptic-curve L-function
accepted_units.why_material: The survey constructs coefficients from point counts modulo primes, builds an Euler product, and invokes modularity to obtain the functional equation, exemplifying how arithmetic geometry produces an RH-type analytic object.
accepted_units.context_note: Because of two-column extraction, the modularity/functional-equation continuation is at lines 499-510 while the curve and coefficient construction is at lines 554-585; unrelated RMT prose lies between them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly display-dependent; exact local factors, shifts, and conductor normalization must be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Modular transformation law generates an L-function with RH symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Ramanujan's product defines Fourier coefficients, modular invariance constrains their generating function, and the resulting Euler product and completed functional equation supply another arithmetic-to-analytic pipeline.
accepted_units.context_note: The right column begins the RMT discussion inside this physical span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transformation law and Euler factors are formula-sensitive; prose establishes the construction's role.

accepted_units.title: Pair correlation identifies the GUE universality class
accepted_units.why_material: Montgomery's normalized zero-pair statistic matches Dyson's Hermitian-matrix correlation function, extending Hilbert-Polya from individual reality to local statistics while explicitly leaving the operator unidentified.
accepted_units.context_note: The left column also finishes modular and elliptic examples before the pair-correlation narrative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The correlation formula and scaling are display-dependent; the identification and its limitation are prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: High-zero computation tests statistical predictions, not RH universally
accepted_units.why_material: A fast evaluation algorithm enabled millions of high zeros to be compared with GUE spacing predictions, giving strong finite statistical agreement at extreme height.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure captions preserve the comparison scale but the plots themselves are unavailable in the text layer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on numerical claims and missing graphics; it is evidence provenance rather than a reusable exact formula.

accepted_units.title: Characteristic polynomials model zeta values and moments
accepted_units.why_material: The random-matrix analogy is lifted from eigenvalue locations to characteristic-polynomial values, where exact Haar averages predict previously mysterious arithmetic-normalized zeta moment constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The extracted order presents the historical resolution before the formal definition of the zeta moments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moment normalizations and the product for g_k are display-dependent; the transfer mechanism is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Families acquire unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic symmetry types
accepted_units.why_material: Katz-Sarnak organize L-function families by monodromy/RMT symmetry, and finite-field proofs show how family geometry can control an individual zeta function, suggesting a family-level route unavailable from isolated-function analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure 9 gives low-zero distribution examples before the prose resumes at line 674.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figure-level empirical comparisons are image-dependent; the symmetry classification and finite-field analogy are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Correct ensemble measure predicts moments, values, and central vanishing
accepted_units.why_material: Using Haar rather than physicists' circular measures produces family-specific moment formulas precise enough to predict value distributions and double-zero frequencies, making the analogy quantitatively falsifiable.
accepted_units.context_note: Two figure captions are interleaved with the prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mathematical claim is prose-grounded, while the plotted validations require the unavailable graphics.

accepted_units.title: Class numbers reduce to L-values and exclusion of near-one zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Dirichlet's class-number formula transforms Gauss's problem into a lower bound for L(1,chi_d), which in turn becomes control of real zeros near 1; Deuring-Heilbronn results reveal that zeros of distinct L-functions constrain one another.
accepted_units.context_note: The page interleaves the class-number development with consequences of a hypothetical exceptional zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The class-number formula and exponents have formula risk, but the reduction chain is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: A hypothetical exceptional zero helps globally while causing ineffectivity locally
accepted_units.why_material: A zero close to 1 forces useful lower bounds or repels zeros of other L-functions, yet assuming its possible existence makes Siegel's bound ineffective; the same obstruction simultaneously creates structure and blocks computation.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines both columns to preserve the full conspiracy mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and exponent bounds are formula-dependent; the logical counterfactual is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Any fixed improvement in a sieve constant would remove the exceptional zero
accepted_units.why_material: The Brun-Titchmarsh theorem sits exactly at constant 2, while lowering it by any absolute amount in a suitable range would force a quantitative exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros, exposing a sharp methodological bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: Class-number material from the other column is interleaved in the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The inequality and parameter range need scan verification; the threshold logic is clearly stated.

accepted_units.title: An implausible half-integer gap model encodes the exceptional-zero obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: The alternative hypothesis predicts normalized consecutive zero gaps near half-integers; disproving it, for example by crossing the half-average-spacing threshold, would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros, but known methods stop essentially at that boundary.
accepted_units.context_note: The transition continues onto the next page and is interleaved with the opening of Iwaniec's approach.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gap normalizations and numerical bounds are formula-dependent; the falsification strategy is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Forced central multiplicity is used to approximate Möbius by family coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Iwaniec proposes families with a forced multiple central zero whose coefficients linearly approximate Möbius, converting RH-style zero control into moment bounds and square-root cancellation for exponential sums.
accepted_units.context_note: The left column simultaneously finishes the gap obstruction and develops modular nonvanishing and Goldfeld's clue.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The family equation, second-moment bound, and incomplete exponential sum are display-heavy and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Exactly fifty percent nonvanishing is insufficient
accepted_units.why_material: Eliminating the Landau-Siegel zero would follow from proving a proportion strictly above one half of a modular L-function family is nonvanishing, while current work reaches exactly one half, making the missing epsilon structurally decisive.
accepted_units.context_note: This is presented as a concrete example of the conspiracy blocking progress at the apparent finish line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; family qualifiers and proportions are clear.

accepted_units.title: A multiple central zero amplifies class-number lower bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Goldfeld's insight is that a simple central zero falls just short but higher multiplicity yields an effective diverging class-number bound; Gross-Zagier's triple-zero examples turn this into a solution of Gauss's problem and motivate extremal families.
accepted_units.context_note: The right column continues Iwaniec's conjectural program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quantitative lower bounds have damaged epsilon/root symbols, but the multiplicity-amplification mechanism is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Classical analytic zero intuition does not transfer to L-functions
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion contrasts regularly spaced zeros of differential-equation special functions with irregular and potentially high-multiplicity L-function zeros, diagnosing why familiar analytic techniques may miss arithmetic phenomena.
accepted_units.context_note: References from the right column begin at line 871 and are interleaved with the mathematical conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The comparison is prose-grounded; the RMT close-pair exponent and multiplicity claims are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: An RH route may require unexplored families and arithmetic geometry
accepted_units.why_material: Conrey argues that families, moment theorems, modularity, exponential-sum estimates, and systematic construction of new L-functions may supply tools that isolated analytic study lacks.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's explicit strategic conclusion, interleaved with bibliography entries.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded and source-opinion qualified; it is a research strategy, not observed proof evidence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-zero and geodesic-spectrum dualities
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Explicit and trace formulas suggest a common duality pattern in which arithmetic primitives correspond to spectral data, but the pseudo-cusp episode shows that analogy must be backed by a legitimate operator and trace identity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source provides resemblance and a cautionary failure, not a construction realizing zeta zeros spectrally.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Equivalent criteria as representation search
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: RH can be transported among prime errors, Möbius cancellation, Hilbert-space approximation, series decay, determinants, and divisor inequalities, making selection of a fertile representation a separate problem from logical equivalence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: No criterion is shown to be easier; the failed Mertens strengthening warns against confusing a sharper-looking proxy with a viable route.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Random matrices: calibrated model, not proof
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The RMT correspondence coherently predicts zero spacings, value moments, family symmetry, and vanishing statistics across analytic, computational, and finite-field evidence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source explicitly says this does not identify the Hilbert-Polya operator or directly lead to a proof of RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exceptional-zero bottlenecks align across methods
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Sieve constants, small zero gaps, family nonvanishing, and class-number effectiveness all meet at sharp thresholds whose slightest improvement would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These equivalences of obstruction do not show which threshold is tractable, and the numerical bounds are source-dated.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Multiplicity and families as an arithmetic amplification strategy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Rather than suppress exotic central zeros, one can choose structured families with forced multiplicity and exploit their coefficients, moments, and arithmetic geometry to amplify weak information into effective bounds.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Iwaniec's reduction still depends on unproved moment and exponential-sum estimates; the proposed extension to RH remains strategic.
